In this opinion article, we argue that kinetoplastid parasites unconventional biology renders them valuable models for understanding spatial regulation of gene expression. We propose that they offer a unique lens through which to explore the functional limits of biomolecular condensates and other membraneless organelles as ‘regulatory hubs’. We propose a broader investigation into whether these organisms utilise conserved condensates with divergent molecular compositions or entirely novel assemblies to drive their life cycle, pathogenesis, and immune evasion. [Trends in Parasitology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1471492226002321).

DOI: 10.1016/j.pt.2026.08.004
